summary: Gérard Colas is an Indologist. He held posts as Directeur de recherche at the CNRS and at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences, and was also attested as a Senior Fellow at the CNRS in 2009.
Gérard Cotton worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Joseph Mansion and earned his Ph.D. from the University of Liège by 1930.

Gérard Devèze was an Indologist and linguist. He studied under Julien Vinson at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales, earning a diploma in Tamil in 1885, and also obtained a diploma from the École Pratique des Hautes Études.

Gérard Fussman (1940–2022) studied at the École Normale Supérieure (circa 1961–1965). A scholar of Indology, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, he headed a section at CNRS (~1969–1984) and became a professor at the Collège de France in 1984.
Gérard Huet works in computational linguistics and Indology. He studied under George Ernst (~1970–1972) and Maurice Nivat (~1972–1976), and served as a professor at Inria from circa 1974 to 2012.

Géza Bethlenfalvy (1936–2021) was a scholar of Tibetology and Indology. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University under János Harmatta and Lajos Ligeti, later holding posts at the University of Delhi, Eötvös Loránd University, and the University of Vienna.

Géza Uray (1921–1991) was a linguist and Tibetologist who studied under Lajos Ligeti. He held academic posts at Eötvös Loránd University, the Research Centre for Linguistics (~1951–1973), and the University of Pennsylvania (1973–1984).

Gösta Liebert (1916–1998) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Lund and Gothenburg under Hjalmar Frisk, Nils Holmer, and Stig Wikander. He held posts at Lund University, Uppsala University, and was a professor at the University of Gothenburg (1955–1982).

Götz von Selle (1893–1956) was a historian who studied in Berlin, Kiel, and Göttingen (Dr. phil. 1920). He held librarian posts at Göttingen and the Royal Library of Berlin, and became an honorary professor and library director at Königsberg in 1939.
Günter Blamberger held a post at the University of Kassel from circa 1990 to 1993, and was appointed Chair in German Philology at the University of Cologne around 1993.

Günter Grönbold is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Helmut Hoffmann (~1964–1969). He held a post at the Bavarian State Library from circa 1974 to 2008, heading its Oriental Section from circa 1988 to 2008.

Günter Lanczkowski (1917–1993) was a religious studies scholar who earned a PhD at Marburg and studied at Göttingen. He served as Privatdocent at Heidelberg (1960–1982) and taught religion at the universities of Mainz (1984–1986) and Munich (1986–1988).

Günter Schweiger is a scholar in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Vienna University of Economics and Business under Gert Klingenschmitt, and served there as a professor (1974–2009) after working at Johannes Kepler University Linz.

Günther Schulemann (1889–1964) worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Berlin, Freiburg, and Breslau (Ph.D. ~1913), where he later served as a Privatdozent (1923) and associate professor of philosophy (1930–1939).

Günther Weibgen (1896–1948) was an Indologist who studied under Heinrich Lüders at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1919–1923). He held posts at the Royal Library of Berlin beginning in 1928, becoming Oberbibliothekar in 1944.

Günther-Dietz Sontheimer (1934–1992) studied Indology and religion at Tübingen under Helmuth von Glasenapp, at ILS Law College, and at SOAS under J. Duncan M. Derrett. He had a long career at Heidelberg University from 1965, becoming a professor in 1979.

H. Craig Melchert is a linguist who studied at Michigan State, the Defense Language Institute, the National Cryptologic School, and Harvard (~1972–1977). He held posts at UNC Chapel Hill (1978–2007) and UCLA (2007–2015).

H. G. Narahari was an Indologist educated at the University of Mysore and the University of Madras, where he completed an M.Litt. by 1943 under C. Kunhan Raja. In 1944, he was a Research Assistant at Adyar Library and a Madras Research Fellow.
H. J. de Graaf (1899–1984) was a historian who studied at Leiden University between circa 1919 and 1935, and studied under Poerbatjaraka from 1927 to 1930.
H. Kikuchi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who was attested in 1966 as a research student at the University of Delhi, studying under Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale.
